messages.text: How to see the live feed when you miner is running

Once it's on your wifi, the miner runs a local dashboard you open in a browser on the same network, by its IP address. That's the live feed: hashrate, shares, temps, pool status, all updating in real time. On our Harlo and Hammer units that's Harlo OS, and you can read the guides and release notes at https://harlolabs.com.

Are you looking at a particular miner, or still deciding? Happy to point you to the right one for where you'd run it.
I have one it's a jingleminer lite

The Solo Lite comes with access to the HeliumDeploy app, and that's where you watch it live: hashrate, shares, uptime. It also runs a local dashboard you can open in a browser on the same wifi, at the miner's IP address from your router's device list.

If it's connected but you can't find it, the fastest help is our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post there and mention @nullhashrate (JD).

Is it already hashing, or are you still getting it on wifi?
It's hashing but i need the live feed

Two ways. Open your router's connected-devices list, find the miner, note its IP, then type that IP into a browser on the same wifi. That's the live dashboard, hashrate and shares updating in real time. Or sign into the HeliumDeploy app, which the Solo Lite comes with, and it shows the same from your phone.

If neither loads, JD can walk you through it. Fastest is Discord right now, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate. Want me to pass it to him here instead?
I don't want to point you at the wrong download, so I'm getting the exact link for the HeliumDeploy app confirmed for you.

The team's on right now, so usually not long. I can't put a clock on it, but they're working the chat today and it lands here or in your email either way.

Discord is the faster bet if you're impatient, JD answers there quickly: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate.

In the meantime the browser route works without the app. Router device list, grab the miner's IP, type it into a browser on the same wifi.
I've tried that but the the website can't be load

Most likely cause: your phone or laptop is on the 5GHz band and the miner is on 2.4GHz, so they can't see each other. Switch your device to the 2.4GHz network, then try the IP again. Type it plain, http://192.168.x.x, no https.
